subject: general
question: What is the ratio between the area of a square having side of 6 cm and that of the rhombus having diagonals of 8 cm and 6 cm?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Area of Square = (Side)² = 6² = 36 cm²

Area of Rhombus = (d₁ × d₂) ÷ 2 = (8 × 6) ÷ 2 = 24 cm²

Required Ratio = 36 : 24 = 3 : 2

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Side of the square (a) = 6 cm

Diagonals of the rhombus (d₁, d₂) = 8 cm and 6 cm

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0fcf199e0f2c8b0a32f250ae35764ee044fcf046b9f78b27f318f455c0be7aa5.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Area of square = a²

Area of rhombus = (d₁ × d₂) ÷ 2

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area of the square = 6 × 6 = 36 cm²

⇒ Area of the rhombus = (8 × 6) ÷ 2 = 24 cm²

⇒ Required Ratio = Area of square : Area of rhombus

⇒ Required Ratio = 36 : 24

⇒ Required Ratio = 3 : 2

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area and Perimeter of a Rhombus

The area of a rhombus is strictly evaluated as half the product of its diagonals: Area = (d₁ × d₂) ÷ 2. The perimeter is 4 × side. Additionally, the relationship between its sides and diagonals is given by: 4a² = d₁² + d₂².

Properties of a Rhombus

All four sides of a rhombus are equal in length. The diagonals bisect each other exactly at right angles (90°), effectively splitting the rhombus into four identical right-angled triangles.

Properties of a Square

A square is simply a specialized rhombus where all interior angles are identically 90°. Its diagonals are completely equal in length and bisect each other at 90° as well. Area = Side² or (Diagonal)² ÷ 2.
